summary: Preinstall hook fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated sibling payload
details: The npm package declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs". setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/, unpacks the binary, and then invokes it via execFileSync against a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a ~727 KB Bun-CJS-compiled bundle whose first line is `// @bun @bun-cjs` and whose body is obfuscator.io-style output (shuffled string array, hex-named `_0x...` identifiers). This is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern: an obfuscated payload is executed under a non-Node runtime fetched at install time, bypassing Node-level static analysis of the installer's tooling. An eslint-config package has no legitimate need for a Bun runtime or a 727 KB obfuscated Bun bundle; the package's advertised purpose (a shared ESLint configuration) cannot account for install-time execution of opaque compiled code with the installer's privileges.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
